To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Gomez <anna@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-sync closure briefing and mandates for QBR runway

Team —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. I captured the key asks from Product & Sales and the exec items we need to lock before QBR. Putting the ask list and owners below so we can converge by EOD Tuesday: 

- Action A (Karthik): finalize the prioritization matrix for the three Customer-facing features (cost/regression/value). Deliverable: single-sheet ranking with tradeoffs.
- Action B (Marissa): consolidate the cross-functional risk register and note mitigation owners. Deliverable: risk table + suggested mitigations.
- Action C (Vivek/Exec): decision on SLA exception for Acme pilot (they asked to reduce cold-start latency to 60ms for dedicated pool). Deliverable: go/no-go + budget delta.
- Action D (Irene): confirm which model variants we can commit to for the demo cadence and whether we can schedule a canary deploy window next week.

Attachments: I exported a starter QBR priorities worksheet (QBR_priorities_v1.xlsx) with the template I used last quarter. Use it as the single source for ranking inputs.

Primary constraints: 1) runway for exec review is next Friday 6/4, 2) we need a final slide deck by Wednesday 6/2 COB, 3) procurement needs preliminary terms to start redlines by Monday 6/7.

Please reply inline with owners marking ETA. If anything is blocked by security/compliance evidence, flag it in the risk register and tag Naomi.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Quick guidance from the exec bench:

1) Acme pilot SLA exception — we should be conservative. I don't want to commit to 60ms if it increases costs >15% for the run. Ask: Marissa/Karthik, please model the customer impact (growth / revenue probability) vs cost delta and present a one-pager.

2) Prioritization — make it binary for exec: must-have / nice-to-have / back-burner. Exec wants a 2-slide rationale per must-have.

3) If there's any ask that requires a contract amendment or price concession, copy Emma in finance and loop procurement.

Please treat these as blocking for my readiness signoff. If you foresee any issue meeting the delivery windows, call it out now.

Vivek
VP, Product

Folks —

Status update and closure notes (closing loop for this thread):

- Action A (Karthik): matrix v1 uploaded to Drive and linked in the QBR workbook. ETA: v2 with perf impacts Tuesday 6/1 11:00 PT.
- Action B (Marissa): risk register consolidated — 6 risks called out (infra quota, procurement timing, compliance evidence, dedicated capacity, model regression, monitoring gaps). Mitigations and owners added in column C. Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2bQBR-runway-priorities
- Action C (Exec/SLA): Vivek asked for customer-impact vs cost delta one-pager. Draft attached (SLA_exception_request.docx). I included preliminary numbers and procurement asked for an initial term sheet placeholder (cc'd procurement).
- Action D (Irene): Can confirm model-variant commitment for the demo: we'll pin to redwood/open-2-small for the on-prem demo and redwood/opt-1 for hosted; canary window scheduled for 6/3 22:00 PT pending infra thumbs-up.

Next steps:
- Karthik: finish perf columns + add one-pager rows for exec.
- Marissa: finalize risk mitigations and hand to Solutions for runbook snippets.
- Irene: collate the two exec slides and drop into the QBR deck by Wed 6/2 18:00 PT.

If there are no objections, I'll mark these actions as "in flight" and move to the QBR master deck. Anna — can you confirm procurement will accept a placeholder term sheet to start redlines?

Thanks —
Marissa
